thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: High packet loss and BGP flap observed for outbound egress via TransitOne to eu-west1 (detected 1768504800-1768504815). Impact: 30% of customer traffic via this path showing >25% packet loss. Auto-remediation attempted and failed. Paging on-call.

Alex G.: Ack. I'm on it. Paging neteng and SRE. Can someone grab traceroute + bgp state? @Priya R. @Carlos M.

Priya R.: Oncall neteng here, looking. Any customer-facing incidents created?

Carlos M.: I started capture from the egress ASBRs. quick checks:
```
# show ip bgp summary | include TransitOne
Neighbor 10.1.2.3    AS 64521    state: established  flaps: 12
Routes advertised: 24K  packets dropped: high
```
Packet loss visible on ASBRs toward TransitOne, spikes coincide with BGP resets.

Alex G.: Thx. Carlos, can you attach the pcap to the INC ticket? Create INC-2026-423 in PagerDuty if not already. Sam, fyi you'll likely pick this up for night.

Sam T.: Got it. I'll standby for handoff if needed.

Priya R.: Quick hypothesis: TransitOne's backbone in eu-west has a partial outage causing route withdraws and route flaps. We should fail traffic to TransitTwo for eu-west prefixes while they stabilize. Suggest: announce /24 more specifics via TransitTwo + set localpref higher toward TransitTwo for affected prefixes.

Carlos M.: Agree. Can push BGP prepends away from TransitOne and advertise more specifics to TransitTwo. But want to throttle to avoid oscillation.

Alex G.: Action plan: 1) Announce /24 specifics for high-volume prefixes via TransitTwo. 2) Set localpref to prefer TransitTwo for those prefixes. 3) If flaps continue, withdraw sessions with TransitOne for affected VRFs. 4) Post customer impact. Who will execute 1-2?

Priya R.: I can push the route announcements and localpref changes. Carlos, coordinate with me on timing so we don't create a routing storm.

Carlos M.: Will coordinate. Preparing commands.

Priya R.: Executing step 1 now. Commands: 
```
# bgp announce more specifics
conf t
router bgp 64500
 network 203.0.113.0/24 route-map ANN-TO-TRANSIT2
exit
route-map ANN-TO-TRANSIT2 permit 10
 set local-preference 200
 set as-path prepend 65000 65000
exit
```
Pushing to edge-rtr-01 -> apply to edge-rtr-02 next.

deploy-bot: deploy job edge-config-update started for edge-rtr-01 (job id 9876).

Alex G.: Monitor convergence after each appliance. Carlos, please run traceroutes to eu-west1 endpoints and check packet loss after announcement.

Carlos M.: Traceroute looks better via TransitTwo after the announce. Packet loss dropped from ~28% to ~3% on observed flows. Still seeing intermittent resets from TransitOne.

Priya R.: Step 2 complete on edge-rtr-01 and edge-rtr-02. localpref bumped. We're seeing route propagation to upstream peers.

Alex G.: Good. Update incident severity: moving from SEV2 -> SEV1 customer-impacting? How many customers affected? Ops team, please tally.

Carlos M.: Quick count from telemetry: ~14 customers had degraded responses for eu-west region (API requests timed out, retries increased). Top 5 customers account for 80% of the impacted traffic.

Alex G.: Marking SEV1. Notify CS and account teams for top 5 customers. Create bridge and post a status page update. Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/912345678 (incident channel).

Priya R.: TransitOne is still flapping. I recommend setting BGP session damping for the affected neighbors to reduce churn locally, and if they don't stabilize in 15m we withdraw the session for affected VRFs.

Carlos M.: Damping applied (local config only) to the specific sessions. Logs: 
```
May 24 22:07:45 bgpd[pid]: neighbor 10.1.2.3 flap suppressed (damping)
```

Alex G.: Good containment. Ops: send customer-facing note: acknowledging connectivity issues to eu-west; now degrading but most traffic routed via backup. ETA to recovery TBD.

Sam T.: Handoff note: I'll take primary on-call at +22:30 UTC. Alex please summarize runbook items I need to continue.

Alex G.: Handoff: 1) Monitor BGP sessions with TransitOne (10.1.2.x) and TransitTwo (10.2.2.x). 2) Watch packet loss telemetry for eu-west prefixes, alert at >10% sustained. 3) Coordinate with NetEng (Priya) for next actions; do not withdraw TransitOne globally unless Priya authorizes. 4) Customer comms: update status page every 15m.

Sam T.: Acknowledged. I've contacted CS for targeted outreach to top 5 customers.

Priya R.: We just got a note from TransitOne NOC: they're seeing an internal peering fabric instability and are engineering a fix, ETA 45m. They asked for us to keep sessions up to maintain traffic via TransitTwo where possible.

Carlos M.: Good intel. Telemetry shows slow improvement in the last 10m. But still some flaps.

Alex G.: Update: we'll keep SEV1 until stable for 1 hour with <1% packet loss. Sam, please continue updates. Priya/Carlos, keep me posted before making any withdraw.

(30m later) Priya R.: TransitOne reports backbone slices recovered. We're seeing stable BGP sessions for 20m. Packet loss down to baseline. I recommend removing localpref changes and retracting extra specifics to avoid sticky routes.

Carlos M.: Rolling back announcements and localpref now. Commands: 
```
no network 203.0.113.0/24 route-map ANN-TO-TRANSIT2
route-map ANN-TO-TRANSIT2 permit 10
 no set local-preference
 no set as-path
exit
```
Applied to edge-rtr-01/02.

deploy-bot: deploy job edge-config-rollback completed (job id 9881).

Alex G.: Monitoring. If stable for 60m we'll post mitigated and close SEV1. Sam, continue monitoring for the window.

Sam T.: Ack. Monitoring active. I'll escalate if anything flaps back.

(60m later) Sam T.: All clear for the 60m stability window. BGP sessions stable, packet loss at baseline. No customer complaints in last hour.

Alex G.: Closing mitigation. Downgrading to SEV3 - postmortem required. Assigning follow-ups:
- Priya: coordinate postmortem with TransitOne NOC and collect their root cause (due in 48h).
- Carlos: attach packet captures and config diffs to INC-2026-423.
- Sam: update status page final note and notify CS/Sales.

Priya R.: Will do. Preliminary note: TransitOne had a peering fabric misconfiguration causing route churn; they will provide RCA.

Carlos M.: Files uploaded to ticket.

Alex G.: Thanks all. Quick retrospective: improve automatic fallback heuristics to reduce customer impact in future (ticket PLAT-789). End of thread.
